question.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{2\times 3}\to R$ defined by $L(A)=3({y}^{T}Ax)$ where 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

What is ${∇}_{A}L$ at 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The gradient of $L$ with respect to $A$ is a matrix of the same shape as $A$, with $(i,j)$th entry given by

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}},
$$

the partial derivative of $L$ with respect to the $(i,j)$th entry of $A.$

Writing out $L$ in component-wise notation as 

$$
L={\sum }_{i=1}^{2}{\sum }_{j=1}^{3}3{a}_{ij}{y}_{i}{x}_{j},
$$

we have

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}=3{y}_{i}{x}_{j}.
$$

Thus, ${∇}_{A}L=3(y\cdot {x}^{T}).$

Evaluating at the given values $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ 7\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
{∇}_{A}L=3([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}])=3([\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 14 \\ 10 & -15 & -35\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-12 & 18 & 42 \\ 30 & -45 & -105\end{aligned}].
$$
